function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on freeways, 35 mph on expressways, 25 mph on city streets.
• “No speed limit” zones exist in some rural areas. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Violations carry a $100 fine plus points. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up or drop off children.
• Failure to stop can lead to a $500 fine. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Drivers must stay in their lane unless turning or merging.
• Lane changes require signaling and checking blind spots. | | **Parking Regulations** | • Parking on sidewalks, crosswalks, or in front of driveways is prohibited.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing is allowed only if the vehicle is unsafe or obstructing traffic.
• Violations can result in a $250 fine. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Annual vehicle inspection required for most vehicles. | | **Points System** | • Traffic violations accrue points on your driver’s license.
• Accumulating 12 points within 3 years can lead to license suspension. | **Where to Find Official Texts** - Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 1–5) - Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) website - Texas Legislature Online (TXLE) for current statutes **Common Enforcement Practices** - Police may issue tickets for speeding, seat‑belt violations, cell‑phone use, and DUI. - Automated enforcement includes speed cameras and red‑light cameras in certain counties. **Recent Updates (2024)** - Texas has introduced stricter penalties for texting while driving. - New regulations require all vehicles to have a functioning seat‑belt reminder system. Feel free to let me know if you need more specific details, such as how to appeal a ticket or the exact wording of a statute!
